documentNotes.title: INSTRUCTIONS
documentNotes.statement:
Look at every page and read the questions carefully.

This multi media test has **30 questions**. You have **45 minutes** to complete the test. If you are ready wait silently until the 45 minutes are over.

Each question is multiple-choice. Choose A, B, C or D. Only one answer is correct.
Some questions contain a short video clip (indicated with [film-reel icon]). Click inside the video frame to start it.

Mark your choice on the Answer Sheet by making a circle around the letter that you want to select. If you make a mistake cross out the selected letter and circle a new choice.

For navigation it is best to use the arrows ↑ ↓ on the keyboard to move to the next page. *Do not click on the escape button, as that ends the presentation.*

Good luck!

documentNotes.title: The End
documentNotes.statement:
You reached the last slide of the multi media test.

Click on the arrow ↑ to go back to the previous page(s) if you want to check your answers.

Or close Adobe Reader.

transcription.notes: Split read (D-P30), chunks 1 and 2 of 2: problems pages 1-24 (cover, instructions, Questions 1-22). Chunk 2 reads pages 25-33 (Questions 23-30 and the closing slide) and the answer sheet (solutions page 1). The paper is a PDF slide presentation with 30 multiple-choice questions, one per slide; each 'Question N' is a separate top-level problem (the catalogue lists 22 problems; the paper prints 30). Cover (page 1) prints 'Edit: Joop van der Schee, Luc Zwartjes'; kept as a document note. Instructions (page 2) contain a film-reel icon that marks video questions; it is written as [film-reel icon], and the arrow symbols as ↑ ↓. Printed 'untill' fixed to 'until'. Kept as printed: Question 7 '21th March 2012' and 'In which direction in the cyclist heading?' ('in' for 'is'); Question 12 'the 2010 Beijing Olympics' (the Beijing Olympics were held in 2008); Question 15 'GDP (Gross Domestic Production)' and 'distribution of :'; Question 16 '1= wave pattern' (no space); Question 9 '32.200 km' (thousands separator as printed); answer options printed without a space after the letter ('A.ESE', 'A.Spain', 'A.The island ...') kept. Question 22 prints 'Espanola' in the options while the map label is 'Española'. Questions 16 and 21 contain a video clip in the original presentation (film-reel icon); only the still frame is in the PDF and is cropped. Line-wrapped answer options are joined into one line. Double spaces in the printed prose were collapsed. Chunk 2: Questions 23-30 (problems pages 25-32), the closing slide 'The End' (page 33, kept as a document note; its arrow symbol written as ↑) and the answer sheet with answer code (solutions page 1), whose red letters give the answer to all 30 questions; each official solution is that answer line. Questions 24 and 26 contain a video clip in the original presentation (film-reel icon); only the still frame is in the PDF and is cropped. Kept as printed: Question 24 and 30 options without a space after the letter ('A.Chicago'); Question 27 'Tonle Sap' and '2,700 km²' / '16,000 km²' (comma thousands separator as printed); Question 30 the column alignment of the options is not kept (spaces collapsed). The answer sheet's Name/Team box and the instruction 'Mark your choice with a circle around the letter:' are part of the blank sheet and are not reproduced.

problems.title: Question 1
problems.statement:
Based on the information in this picture, in which direction away from Amsterdam was this plane flying?

A. North

B. South

C. East

D. West

figures.caption: Photo: Jussi Mestari
figures.alt: Photo of an in-flight information screen titled 'Flight Information' listing: Time to Destination 8:26; Estimated Time of Arrival 1:16 PM; Local Time at Destination 4:50 AM; Local Time at Amsterdam 1:50 PM.

problems.title: Question 2
problems.statement:
Where was this picture taken?

A. 35° S in Africa

B. 35° S in Australia

C. 60° S in South America

D. 60° N in Europe

figures.caption: photo: Jussi Mestari
figures.alt: Night photo of a blue signpost in front of an old building: one arm reads '6131Km SOUTH POLE', another reads 'BUENOS AIRES 6456Km', a third partly hidden arm reads '1231Km'.

problems.title: Question 3
problems.statement:
The map shows worldwide production of

A. Grapes

B. Wheat

C. Rice

D. Cotton

figures.alt: World choropleth map in shades of blue from the UNEP Environmental Data Explorer (credit line 'UNEP/DEWA/GRID-Geneva, UNEP Environmental Data Explorer'); the darkest classes cover the USA, Brazil, China, India, South-East Asia and Egypt; Russia and Argentina are dark blue, Australia medium blue.
Map legend: LEGEND; International Boundaries; Units: Metric Tons; no data; 1100 to 41929; 41929 to 173074; 173074 to 750000; 750000 to 4523690; 4523690 to 197257000.

problems.title: Question 4
problems.statement:
What is the main rock of this landform?

A. Basalt

B. Tuff

C. Limestone

D. Granite

figures.alt: Photo of a valley with many pale cone-shaped rock pinnacles ('fairy chimneys') in front of a town built among similar rock formations.

problems.title: Question 5
problems.statement:
Which of the figures explains the phenomenon of clouds in the mountains as shown on the photograph?

A, B, C or D ?

figures.alt: Four schematic cross-sections A, B, C, D of two green mountains with a valley between them, E on the left and W on the right; each shows a yellow sun, dark arrows and a small cloud over the right-hand (western) peak. A: sun above the left peak, arrows pointing down into the valley. B: sun at upper right, arrows pointing down-left from the right peak into the valley. C: sun above the valley, arrows pointing straight down. D: sun in the valley, arrows pointing up toward the cloud on the right peak.
Photo of a forested rocky mountain slope with a band of cloud lying along the slope under a blue sky.

problems.title: Question 6
problems.statement:
Which two islands are main areas of cultivation for the depicted crop:

A. Sri Lanka and Java

B. Midway and Mauritius

C. The Azores and Sumatra

D. Hokkaido and New Guinea

figures.alt: Photo of a hilly plantation of low, neatly trimmed green bushes covering the slopes, with a road winding between trees and a cow on the road.

problems.title: Question 7
problems.statement:
The picture shows Yverdon-les-Bains in Switzerland (46° 46.71′ N and 6° 38.45′E). It was taken on 21th March 2012. In which direction in the cyclist heading?

A.ESE

B.WNW

C.ENE

D.WSW

figures.alt: Sunny photo of a town square with a baroque church façade with a clock, a building labelled 'BAZAR D'YVERDON' on the left, a couple posing in front, and a cyclist riding away from the camera toward the church; shadows fall toward the viewer.

problems.title: Question 8
problems.statement:
With what stage of the demographic transition does this population histogram correspond?

A. Stage 1

B. Stage 2

C. Stage 3

D. Stage 4

figures.alt: Population pyramid with MALE on the left and FEMALE on the right, age groups 0-4 to 85+, x-axis 'Population (in millions)' from 5 to 0 to 5; the bars are narrow at the base (about 2 million per sex), widest around ages 30-39 (about 3.6-4 million) and narrow at the top. Source line: 'Source: U.S. Census Bureau, International Data Base.'

Demographic transition model: y-axis 'Birth/death rates', x-axis 'Time', divided by dashed lines into Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, Stage 4; the birth rate and death rate curves start high and fluctuating, the death rate falls in Stage 2, the birth rate falls in Stage 3, both are low in Stage 4; the shaded area between them is labelled 'Natural increase'.

problems.title: Question 9
problems.statement:
We leave Sydney in the indicated direction. Which city will we reach after 32.200 km:

A. Singapore

B. Paris

C. Tokyo

D. New York

figures.alt: Google Earth view of Australia with a graticule (labels E105° to E165°, S15° to S45°) and the Tropic of Capricorn marked 'Steenbokskeerkring'; a placemark 'Sydney Nieuw-Zuid-Wales, Australië' with a red arrow pointing due south from Sydney; north arrow at top right.

problems.title: Question 10
problems.statement:
The photo shows a building in Jakarta constructed by the Dutch. Remnants from colonial times can still be seen in many countries. For which country is this not true?

A. Thailand

B. Canada

C. Laos

D. Libya

figures.alt: Photo of a white colonial building with a red tiled roof, green shutters and a domed cupola, with a crowd of people and motorcycles in front.

problems.title: Question 11
problems.statement:
In what country were these photos taken?

A. Cape Verde

B. Cuba

C. Tonga

D. Sri Lanka

figures.alt: Photo of a ceremony on a lawn: a black canopy marked 'GT' with a crown over a draped coffin, surrounded by many people in black wearing woven mats around their waists and rows of people in blue.
Photo of a white church with a cross under a cloudy sky, palm trees, and people seated on mats in front; a small red-and-white flag with a red cross in the foreground.
Photo of a village road lined with power poles and tropical trees, two schoolchildren with backpacks walking, and pigs crossing the road.

problems.title: Question 12
problems.statement:
What does this world map show the distribution of?

A. Total number of internet connections

B. Medals won at the 2010 Beijing Olympics

C. Total numbers of tourist arrivals

D. Number of dentists per thousand population

figures.alt: Bubble cartogram of the world in which each country is a circle sized by value, coloured by continent; the largest circles are United States, China, Russia, Britain, Germany, France and Australia; other labelled circles: Canada, Cuba, Brazil, Spain, Italy, Poland, Belarus, Ukraine, Japan, South Korea, Kenya.

problems.title: Question 13
problems.statement:
Which city has the same type of road network as Moscow?

A. Kyoto

B. Cairo

C. Paris

D. Chicago

figures.alt: German-language road map of Moscow showing a radial-concentric pattern: roads radiating from the centre (Kreml, Roter Pl.) crossed by ring roads, with the outer ring motorway in red; districts labelled in German transliteration (e.g. Putilkowo, Tuschino, Ostankino, Ismajlowo, Ljuberzy, Tjoplyj Stan); legend 'Geschlossene Bebauung', 'Lockere Bebauung'.

problems.title: Question 14
problems.statement:
Red/blue circles on this map indicate the location of severe damage caused by a type of natural hazard in 2008-2010.
This hazard was:

A. Earthquakes

B. Mud flows

C. Floods

D. Tsunamis

figures.alt: Map of South Asia and the Hindu Kush-Himalaya region (Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar, China, Thailand, Laos) with red circles (Killed) and blue circles (Affected, thousands) sized by number; the largest circles are in Pakistan along the Indus and in eastern India/Bangladesh. Legend: Hindu Kush-Himalaya region, Glaciers, Lakes; circle sizes Killed 1 000, 300, 50, 10; Affected (Thousands). Note: data for both killed and affected people may not be available for all the events shown. Sources: ICIMOD, Information on the Occasion of World Environment Day, 2007; ICIMOD online database, accessed July 2010; OCHA, 2010; BBC Press review, 2010.

problems.title: Question 15
problems.statement:
This early 21st century world map shows the geographical distribution of :

A. Average life expectancy

B. GDP (Gross Domestic Production)

C. Literacy

D. Primary education

figures.alt: Cartogram of the world in which country areas are distorted by value: North America, Western Europe and 'Japan and South Korea' are hugely enlarged in red, while Africa, South America and South Asia are shrunk and shown in pale or blue shades.

problems.title: Question 16
problems.statement:
Which words are missing in the text below?

A. 1 = *climate change* and 2 = *is not broken down*

B. 1= *wave pattern* and 2 = *accumulates*

C. 1 = *rotation of the earth* and 2 = *accumulates*

D. 1 = *distance to the equator* and 2 = *is not broken down*

*The oceans are dynamic systems, made up of complex networks of currents that keep water circulating around the World. The direction of the currents is determined by wind, variations in water density and ……………………(1). Sometimes this creates ocean currents that take on enormous circular motion. These are called gyres. Due to the deflection of ocean currents at the centre of the gyre, plastic debris .……………………………. (2).*

figures.alt: Still from a video clip: world ocean map in shades of blue showing modelled concentration of floating debris, with pale accumulation zones in the centres of the subtropical gyres of the Pacific and Atlantic; credit 'Gyre Model: Nikolai Maximenko' and a partly cut label 'ear # 0.67'.

problems.title: Question 17
problems.statement:
The central feature in this photo was formed by:

A. Erosion of a ring dyke

B. Impact of a meteorite

C. Volcanic eruption

D. Uplift of a concave slope

figures.alt: Aerial photo of a large circular crater with a raised rim in flat arid red-orange terrain, with a green vegetated patch in its centre.

problems.title: Question 18
problems.statement:
The Cabinet of which island country held an underwater meeting to draw attention to the threat of rising sea level submerging their country?

A. Maldives

B. Fiji

C. Malta

D. Iceland

figures.alt: Photo of a group of people in scuba gear standing in shallow turquoise sea water next to a quay, with a boom microphone above them.

problems.title: Question 19
problems.statement:
There are two landlocked countries in South America, but only one of them has a capital that cannot be reached by ship from the ocean. Which country is it?

A. Peru

B. Bolivia

C. Paraguay

D. Uruguay

figures.alt: Satellite image of South America on a tilted rounded tile, with no borders or labels.

problems.title: Question 20
problems.statement:
Here are three models characterizing the development of urban processes. This reduction of complexity allows an easier analysis of urban forms. Look carefully. Which name does not refer to one of these three models?

A. Concentric model (after Burgess)

B. Sector model (after Hoyt)

C. Multiple nuclei model (after Harris and Ullman)

D. Multiple segment model (after Lloyd)

figures.alt: Concentric-ring urban model: a red centre surrounded by rings, with the key 1 Loop; 2 Factory zone; 2 Zone in transition; 3 Zone of working men's homes; 4 Residential zone; 5 Commuters' zone.
Urban model made of irregular blocks numbered 1 to 9: a red centre 1, orange 2, yellow 3 areas, a large green 4, teal 5, and separate small squares 6, 7, 8 and 9.
Urban model of wedge-shaped sectors radiating from a red centre 1: orange sectors 2, yellow sectors 3, green sectors 4 and a teal sector 5.

problems.title: Question 21
problems.statement:
Which country’s data makes the blue line?

A.Spain

B.Indonesia

C.Ecuador

D.Botswana

figures.alt: Still from a video clip of a Gapminder World (April 7, 2011) bubble chart at year 1800: y-axis 'Life expectancy (years)' 25 to 85, x-axis 'Income per person (GDP/capita, PPP dollars inflation-adjusted)' on a log scale 200 to 40 000; a cloud of faint bubbles near life expectancy 25-40 and four highlighted bubbles (blue, red, yellow, orange) with trails; a time slider 1800-2000 and a Play button below.

problems.title: Question 22
problems.statement:
This satellite picture shows the volcanic Galapagos Islands. Which of the following statements is correct?

A.The island of Isabela is older than Santa Fé.

B.The island of San Cristobal is younger than Fernandina.

C.The island of Isabela is younger than the island of Espanola.

D.The island of Espanola is younger than the island of Isabela.

figures.alt: Satellite image of the Galápagos Islands with labels: Pinta, Marchena, Genovesa, Santiago, Bartolomé, Rábida, Seymour Norte, Baltra, Plaza Sur, Santa Cruz, Fernandina, Isabela, Pinzón, Tortuga, Santa Fé, San Cristobal, Floreana, Española.

problems.statement:
Which natural product is native to Ethiopia, but was a commercial success in South America?

A. Coffee

B. Cocoa

C. Orange

D. Tea

figures.alt: Close-up photo of a shrub with glossy, dark green, lance-shaped leaves with deep veins and clusters of small white flowers at the leaf axils.

problems.title: Question 24

This film zooms out from which city?

A.Chicago

B.Montreal

C.New York

figures.alt: Still frame of the video (black bars above and below): aerial view straight down on a pier ending in a round plaza with concentric circular structures, surrounded by turquoise water; a road and parking area lead to it from the left.

problems.title: Question 25
problems.statement:
The map shows a population growth rate of over 2% for Sub-Saharan Africa. What is the reason for the zero growth rate in South Africa?

A. Improved level of education

B. High standard of living

C. HIV pandemic

D. Climate change

figures.alt: World map of population growth rate by country with the legend 3+, 2, 1, 0-1, -0 (yellow, green, light blue, dark blue, purple): most of Sub-Saharan Africa is green or yellow; South Africa, Russia and much of Europe are purple; North America, China and Australia dark blue; South America and India light blue.

problems.title: Question 26
problems.statement:
Forest fires in Mediterranean countries like Portugal are often caused by:

A. Strong winds coming from the Atlantic Ocean

B. People who set fire to areas on purpose or accidentally

C. Spontaneous ignition when there is a combination of high temperatures and dry weather in the summer

D. Sparks coming from passing cars

figures.alt: Still frame of a euronews video (logo top right): a bright glare of fire and smoke filling most of the frame, with a tree trunk and vegetation at the left edge.

problems.title: Question 27
problems.statement:
Which word is missing in the text below?

A. Spring

B. Monsoon

C. Snow melt

D. Autumn

*The Tonle Sap remains relatively small for most of the year, measuring about a metre in depth and covering around 2,700 km². However, the river connected to the lake starts to swell during the …………… season as water that flows from the Mekong River reverses, helping to expand the Tonle Sap to an area of up to 16,000 km² with a depth of up to 9 metres.*

figures.alt: Map of Cambodia with provinces (Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Stung Treng, Ratanakiri, Bantey Meanchey, Siem Reap, Battambang, Pailin, Kampong Thom, Kratie, Mondolkiri, Pursat, Kampong Chhnang, Kampong Cham, Kampong Speu, Koh Kong, Prey Veng, Svay Rieng, Kandal, Takeo, Kampot, Sihanoukville), the lake Tonle Sap and the Mekong river in blue, the capital Phnom Penh, neighbouring THAILAND, LAOS and VIETNAM, the Gulf of Thailand and the South China Sea, and a scale bar 0–50 mi / 0–50 km.

problems.title: Question 30
problems.statement:
Walls and fences are everywhere in the world. Where were these pictures taken?

A. 1 = Belfast, 2 = Tijuana, 3 = Paju

B. 1 = Paju, 2 = Tijuana, 3 = Belfast

C. 1 = Paju, 2 = Belfast, 3 = Tijuana

D. 1 = Tijuana, 2 = Paju, 3 = Belfast

figures.alt: Photo labelled '1': a tall rusty metal fence of vertical posts running across a sandy beach far into the sea, with a few people on the beach.
Photo labelled '2': a fence topped with coils of barbed wire, covered with many colourful ribbons; people lean on it, looking at the ribbons.
Photo labelled '3': view over a town of brick houses with a long high wall/fence running through a residential area; small credit line '© Alison Leigh Lilly' in the corner.
